title: Many Perturbations, Shared Failure Dynamics: Tracing Direction-Sensitive Perturbation Influence in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.32309v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Why can a task-preserving rewrite turn a correct answer into a failure while a larger internal change leaves the answer intact? We develop a direction-sensitive, readout-relative account of semantic fragility: heterogeneous language changes can share geometric and readout relationships without sharing an input-independent failure direction. Clean decision reserve, representation transformation, and response alignment provide complementary descriptions of this process. An exact longitudinal-transverse decomposition identifies directional information discarded by scalar transmission. A compact reserve-and-transmission model predicts failures across held-out families and items in Qwen3-32B and Gemma 4 31B, with useful but parameterization-dependent transfer to ReClor. Matched interventions show that orientation carries causal information beyond scalar geometry. Among naturally failed rewrites, attention-component tests on disjoint original

translated_title: 多种扰动，共享的失败动力学：追踪语言模型中方向敏感的扰动影响
translated_abstract: 为什么一次保持任务语义的改写会把正确答案变成失败，而更大的内部变化却让答案保持不变？我们提出了一种方向敏感的、相对于读出过程的语义脆弱性解释：异质的语言变化可以共享几何与读出关系，而不必共享一个与输入无关的失败方向。干净的决策储备、表示变换和响应对齐为这一过程提供了互补的描述。一个精确的纵-横分解识别出被标量传输所丢弃的方向信息。一个紧凑的储备-传输模型在 Qwen3-32B 和 Gemma 4 31B 上对留出的族群和条目实现了失败预测，并向 ReClor 实现了有用但依赖参数化方式的迁移。匹配干预实验表明，扰动的方向携带了超越标量几何的因果信息。在自然发生的失败改写中，针对不相交原始样本的注意力组件测试……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种方向敏感、相对于读出过程的语义脆弱性分析框架，通过纵-横分解与储备-传输模型揭示异质扰动在语言模型中共享相同的失败动力学，并证明扰动的方向（而不仅是标量大小）携带因果信息。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a direction-sensitive, readout-relative account of semantic fragility, showing via an exact longitudinal-transverse decomposition and a compact reserve-and-transmission model that heterogeneous task-preserving perturbations share common failure dynamics across language models (Qwen3-32B, Gemma 4 31B), with matched interventions demonstrating that perturbation orientation carries causal information beyond scalar geometry.
